faq: Do I need an existing phone app?
Yes. These layouts extend an app you already have, so we need the project source. If you have no app yet, order an Android build and we plan tablet and watch screens into it.
Will tablet layouts matter for my Play listing?
Google publishes large screen app quality guidelines, and we build to them. We cannot promise any store placement, but we do prepare tablet screenshots for your listing.
Can the Wear OS app run without the phone?
It can for simple features, but most useful watch apps sync with the phone app. We explain the tradeoff and build whichever fits your use case, within the package limit.
Which devices do you test on?
We use Android Studio emulators for phone, tablet, foldable and watch sizes, and real devices where we have them. If you must support a specific model, tell us and we check it.
desc:
Ecom Swift LLC offers tablet, foldable and Wear OS app development: adaptive layouts for large screens and folding phones, plus companion watch screens and tiles, so your Android app fits every device it runs on.

## What is tablet, foldable and Wear OS app development?

It is the work of making an Android app behave well beyond a single phone size. For tablets and foldables, that means layouts that use extra width, such as a list beside its detail view. For watches, it means a small, focused Wear OS app, and often a tile that shows key information at a glance.

Android runs on phones, tablets, folding devices, watches and Chromebooks. One stretched phone screen rarely suits all of them.

## Why large screens and watches need their own design

A phone layout on a tablet wastes space. Buttons stretch across the screen, text lines grow too long to read and the user taps through three screens for what could sit side by side. On a foldable, the app must respond when the device opens, closes or stands half-bent.

Watches are different again. The screen is tiny, interactions last seconds and users glance rather than read. An app that copies its phone interface onto a wrist feels clumsy. Google Play also treats large screen quality as part of how apps are judged, so careless layouts can hurt how your app is presented on those devices.

## How adaptive design affects users

On larger screens, people stay longer and do more complex tasks: reading, writing, comparing, editing. A good tablet layout supports that with panes, keyboard shortcuts and mouse input. Users who start on a phone and continue on a tablet then find the experience familiar.

A watch app serves quick moments: a timer, a reminder, a workout step, a delivery status. It reduces the need to pull out the phone. We cannot promise installs on these devices, as that depends on your audience, but a proper fit makes the app welcome there.

## What a strong adaptive app includes

- Window size classes, so the layout responds to the space it has.
- List and detail panes on tablets and in landscape.
- Landscape and split-screen support that does not break state.
- Foldable posture handling, such as table-top mode.
- Keyboard and mouse support for tablets and Chromebooks.
- Touch targets and text sized for each form factor.
- Large screen screenshots ready for the Play listing.
- A Wear OS app with a few clear screens, written for round and square watches.
- A Wear OS tile that shows the most useful information.
- Data sync between the phone and the watch.

## How we work

We start with your current app and ask which screens matter on larger devices. Then we adapt them one at a time and test on tablet and foldable emulators, and on real devices where available. For Wear OS, we design a small set of watch screens and a tile, connect them to the phone app and test on small and large watch emulators.

The Basic package adapts your top screens and delivers an internal test build. Standard covers a fuller tablet experience with list and detail panes, input support, foldable handling and screenshots. Premium adds a companion Wear OS app and tile with phone to watch sync.

## Practical guidance

**Do:**
- Decide which tasks suit a watch before drawing any screen.
- Keep the phone app as the source of truth for data.
- Test with the window resized, rotated and split.
- Support keyboard navigation on larger screens.
- Provide screenshots made for each device type.

**Avoid:**
- Locking the app to portrait on every device.
- Placing long text blocks on a watch face.
- Assuming every foldable behaves the same way.
- Copying the phone navigation onto a tablet without change.
- Releasing watch features that need a phone connection without telling the user.

## Who this is for

An owner whose app looks stretched and awkward on tablets. A productivity or media app that would gain from list and detail layouts. A fitness, delivery or reminder app whose users would value a glance on the wrist. A business that sells to schools or offices where tablets and Chromebooks are common.

## What we need from you

Send the current app or source code, a short note on which devices matter and a test account. Source access is given as a collaborator invite, and Play Console access as a limited user. We never need passwords. A phone app is not required to begin with Wear OS, though a companion usually relies on one.
